one_liner: JVM build tool for Java/Scala/Kotlin; 4-44x faster clean/incremental compiles than Maven, 3.6-10.2x than Gradle.
what_it_does: Mill replaces Maven's pom.xml and Gradle's build.gradle with a declarative build.mill (Scala-like DSL, or build.mill.yaml) for JVM projects. It handles dependency resolution (via Coursier), compilation, testing, and packaging for Java, Scala, and Kotlin modules. It is not a drop-in for existing pom.xml/build.gradle files: adopting it means porting the build definition to Mill's own module/task model.
how_it_is_fast: Mill runs a persistent JVM background daemon, avoiding per-invocation JVM startup and classloading. It memoizes every build step as a fine-grained Task in a dependency graph, so unchanged tasks are skipped entirely (no-op compiles finish in ~0.1s). For Java/Scala incremental compiles it uses the Zinc incremental compiler to recompile only files whose changes affect downstream code. Unlike Maven, it works directly with classfiles on disk rather than round-tripping through .m2 jar packing/unpacking, and it parallelizes independent tasks by default.
when_to_use: Multi-module Java/Scala/Kotlin monorepos where edit-compile-test iteration speed matters
CI pipelines bottlenecked by Maven/Gradle daemon startup or full-module recompilation on every run
Teams that want built-in selective test execution, test parallelism, and Chrome-trace build profiling without extra plugins
New JVM projects willing to adopt a non-XML/non-Groovy build DSL from the start
Want a self-contained native (Graal) launcher with fast CLI startup and no local JDK requirement
when_not_to_use: Large existing Maven/Gradle codebase with heavy reliance on the Maven Central/Gradle Plugin Portal plugin ecosystem, which Mill's is much smaller than
Non-JVM projects (C++/CMake/Cargo, etc.) - not applicable at all
Windows-ARM machines: Mill has no native executable there (upstream GraalVM limitation) and falls back to the slower JVM launcher, which also needs a system JDK 17+
Teams running very high task parallelism on newer Mill versions: an open issue (#7381, 1.2.0-RC1) reports up to ~20x slowdown and thread-pool blowup at large --jobs values
Projects needing mature BSP/IDE tooling parity - several Metals/BSP integration bugs have been filed (mostly closed, but recent)

integration.form: source-drop (CLI tool + build.mill config file per project, not a library)
integration.dependencies: none for the default launcher (self-contained Graal native binary, downloads its own JVM for module builds); the '-jvm' launcher variant requires a system JDK 17+
integration.min_toolchain: Mill supports JVM 11+ for evaluating builds (configurable per-project via mill-jvm-version); native launcher needs no local JDK, JVM launcher needs JDK 17+
integration.platforms: Native executables: Windows/Mac/Linux on Intel, Mac/Linux on ARM. Windows-ARM has no native executable and falls back to the JVM launcher.
integration.thread_safety: not documented (CLI build tool, not a library); parallel task execution is a first-class feature but internal thread-safety guarantees for custom task code aren't specified
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial - Mill provides MavenModule/other traits to ease porting, and a `mill init` scaffolder, but existing pom.xml/build.gradle files must still be manually ported to build.mill

gotchas: PowerShell 5.1 writes UTF-16LE .mill-version files that Mill can't read; PowerShell 7+ is required on Windows
Benchmark page itself is internally inconsistent on the Mill version used: the summary text says 'Mill 1.1.0' while the detailed benchmark tables specify 'Java 17 + Mill 0.12.9-native'
The Netty and Mockito ports used for the benchmark are not 100% complete - some subprojects, linters, and Android/Kotlin/OSGI tests were disabled to make the comparison apples-to-apples
Open bug (#7381) shows severe negative performance scaling (thread pool grows to thousands of blocked threads) at very high --jobs counts on a 1.2.0-RC1 build; unclear if it reached a stable release
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No sibling overlap: ccache, Buck2, tup, and xmake all target C/C++ or polyglot native builds, not the JVM. Pick Mill specifically when the baseline pain is Maven/Gradle overhead on a Java/Scala/Kotlin project; none of the catalogued siblings apply there.
verified_claims_summary: Mill's own docs page (mill-build.org/mill/comparisons/performance.html) benchmarked Mill 0.12.9-native (Java 17) against each project's default Maven/Gradle version on a 2021 M1 MacBook Pro (10 CPU, 32GB RAM), median wall time of 3 runs after warmup. Netty (~500k LOC, 47 modules) vs Maven: 4.0x-44.0x across sequential/parallel/single-module clean, incremental, and no-op compile. Mockito (~100k LOC, 22 modules) vs Gradle: 3.6x-10.2x for the same five scenarios.
status_note: Actively maintained: latest commit is today (2026-09-24), 2.8k GitHub stars, MIT licensed. Distributed as a self-updating bootstrap script (Maven Central-hosted releases), so it's directly usable without vendoring.
